newsitem.title: GERMANY: WAIGEL TO CURB GERMAN SPENDING, BILD SAYS.
newsitem.headline: WAIGEL TO CURB GERMAN SPENDING, BILD SAYS.

text.p: Finance Minister Theo Waigel will clamp down on German government spending after announcing that last year's federal deficit badly overshot budget targets, the Bild tabloid reported on Thursday.
Bild said that Waigel would announce a spending freeze on January 28, with ministers having to seek individual approval for any items exceeding 500,000 marks.

Waigel wants to bring the total public sector deficit below the Maastricht treaty's target of three percent of gross domestic product this year so that Germany can qualify for European monetary union in 1999.
The overall deficit was 3.9 percent of GDP in 1996. Federal borrowing last year overshot budget targets by 18.4 billion marks to hit 78.3 billion marks, Waigel said on Wednesday.
